holidays.name: National Bow Tie Day
holidays.description: A day for flipping your collar and tying on a little whimsy. Bow ties get their moment, whether you wear a classic silk one, a polka-dot one, or a clip-on you hope nobody checks. Dapper professors, magicians, and dessert-table waiters are all invited to the party.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on the fashion and menswear calendar, and it encourages everyone to add a bit of neckwear flair.
holidays.funFact: The bow tie is often said to descend from scarves that Croatian mercenaries wore in the 17th century. That story is also the traditional explanation for why the necktie is called a 'cravat.'

holidays.name: Race Your Mouse Around the Icons Day
holidays.description: A playful salute to the humble computer mouse. Take your cursor for a victory lap around your desktop icons, weaving and swerving like a tiny digital race car. It is the one day when procrastinating at your computer counts as a celebration.
holidays.origin: This is a tongue-in-cheek observance from the quirky holiday creators Thomas and Ruth Roy of Wellcat Holidays. It is meant to bring some fun to the workday.
holidays.funFact: Douglas Engelbart demonstrated the first computer mouse prototype in 1968. It was a wooden shell with a single button, and he reportedly nicknamed it a 'mouse' because the cord looked like a tail.

holidays.name: Power Rangers Day
holidays.description: Fans of the Mighty Morphin franchise celebrate with a morphin' marathon. Expect karate kicks, color-coded spandex, giant robot battles, and plenty of cries of 'It's morphin' time!' It is a nostalgic day for anyone who grew up on after-school heroics.
holidays.origin: The observance honors the franchise's TV debut. Mighty Morphin Power Rangers first aired in the United States on August 28, 1993.
holidays.funFact: The original series used footage from the Japanese show Super Sentai. The producers filmed new scenes with American actors and spliced them into the Japanese action footage.
